capture_boundary.meaning: MessageController.Send intercepts every outbound protocol message before the wrapped environment Transport is reached; in capture mode it records a stable snapshot and suppresses the original send.

pending_store.meaning: pending map keyed by message ID (msg-<CaptureSequence>), guarded by MessageController.mu

entrypoint.meaning: single outbound funnel: every outbound protocol message (heartbeats, vote requests, append entries, responses) reaches MessageController.Send through the node's Transport here.

message_capture.copy_strategy: deep clone via Message.Clone at capture time; ListPending returns fresh deep clones so the pending store is never mutated
message_capture.production_mode: production mode (default): Send forwards the message unchanged to the wrapped Transport
message_capture.test_mode: capture mode (SetCaptureMode(true)/EnableCapture): Send stores a stable snapshot in the pending store and returns nil, suppressing the original send
notes: NewMessageController(Transport) wraps the environment-owned transport; capture mode is off by default (production mode forwards unchanged).

In capture mode Send assigns a per-instance CaptureSequence and an ID of the form msg-<CaptureSequence>, stores a Message.Clone() snapshot, and returns nil so the message never continues along the original uncontrollable send path.
ListPending() returns stable metadata (ID, From, To, Type, CaptureSequence plus full message snapshot) ordered by CaptureSequence; ClearPending() removes all pending messages.
Test-controller operations (Inject, ListPending, ClearPending) are serialized by a dedicated opMu; outbound capture only takes the store mutex and may occur concurrently with them.
The recorded target node is resolved at capture time (controller registry, with fallback to the wrapped transport's read-only Node(id) accessor) so injection is deterministic.
Nodes created with the controller as their Transport self-register via NewNode; explicit Register/Unregister are also available.

pending_store.meaning: pending map keyed by message ID (msg-<CaptureSequence>), guarded by MessageController.mu

entrypoint.meaning: normal protocol input boundary: verifies To == node.id, processes synchronously under the mutex, and clones the message before handling it

message_injection.copy_strategy: injected message is rebuilt from the stored snapshot with fresh entry clones; Node.Step clones it again before processing, so content is never mutated
message_injection.production_mode: no injection in production mode; Inject only applies to messages captured by the same controller instance
message_injection.test_mode: test mode: Inject delivers a captured message through the recorded target's Node.Step and consumes it only on nil error, leaving it pending on failure
notes: Inject(messageID) selects a pending message by ID, uses the recorded target (captured at Send time, re-resolved at Inject time), and delivers it through the target's normal Node.Step boundary.

The message is consumed (removed from the pending store) only after delivery succeeds; on any delivery error (ErrPaused, ErrUnknownNode) it remains pending, and an unknown ID returns ErrUnknownMessage without side effects.
Inject, ListPending, and ClearPending are serialized via opMu; outbound capture may occur concurrently. No IN_FLIGHT state was introduced for concurrent Inject calls.
Outbound messages produced while processing an injected message re-enter the same capture funnel (capture mode) or the wrapped transport (production mode).
message_id_scope is pending_store_instance: IDs are unique within the MessageController instance that captured the message.
